17.text: Reindeer-moss grows throughout the year, but, if too much trampled upon,

18.text: it will wither and dry up. Such spoiled pastures are exceedingly slow in

19.text: recovering, and they sometimes remain waste for more than twenty years.

20.text: The same is true of districts that are burnt over.

21.text: Reindeer cannot remain too long at one place, since the constant scraping

22.text: of their hoofs hardens the snow, and it becomes difficult to reach the moss

23.text: under it. Large herds especially have to move forward after a few hours,

24.text: and actually keep moving the whole winter. Therefore the animals in very

25.text: large herds do not have much fat. A pasture, after having been grazed over

26.text: for a day or two, is useless till the next year, and will not be resorted to

27.text: again in the same season. A pasture that has been used for three or four

28.text: successive years has to be given a rest for five or six years. Thus reindeer-

29.text: herds will thrive only when the available grounds are large enough for a

30.text: continuous change of good pastures, carefully picked out among the vast spaces

31.text: of poor land and coarse fodder. The summer pastures are not so easily

32.text: exhausted; and on the Arctic seashore, between the Kolyma and Chaun,

33.text: although resorted to every year for half a century, they still thrive, and sprout

34.text: again every spring. The best strip of pasture-land here lies close to the shore,

35.text: and is usually occupied by poor people, who quite overcrowd it, — at least
